title: Cohort-adaptive steward batcher and KV fragmentation solver for mixed-length workloads
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current continuous batcher degrades under mixed prompt/response length distributions: long-turn conversations produce KV cache fragmentation and excessive GPU slab retention, while short interactive prompts suffer elevated tail latency from late coalescing. Goal: design and land a scheduler variant (the 'cohort-adaptive steward') that groups requests into transient cohorts by estimated horizon and memory footprint, applies KV compaction heuristics per cohort, and dynamically adjusts slot tenure to reduce GPU memory fragmentation without increasing 95th/99th latency for short requests.

Scope: scheduler + admission control + KV eviction policy changes; no inference kernels. Must be safe behind runtime feature flag and default to current scheduler if disabled.

Success metrics (primary):
- 95th percentile latency for short (<64 token) requests: not degraded (>+2% allowed)
- 99th percentile latency overall: -10% relative improvement target
- GPU resident memory fragmentation (measured as free-slab ratio): -12% relative improvement
- Effective throughput (tokens/s/GPU) at 95th latency SLO: +6% relative improvement

Acceptance criteria:
1) Data-backed experiment showing repeatable gains on mixed production-like traces (see experiment_results).
2) Feature-flagged rollout path + canary plan in runtime-1.22 release docs.
3) Benchmarks and tracing hooks to attribute latency and eviction events per cohort.

Design summary:
- Admission/cohorting: incoming requests are given a lightweight horizon estimate based on prompt tokens, user history length, and model-reply size prediction. Requests are assigned to fast/medium/long cohorts. Cohorts are elastic: each has a target batch window and a max slot tenure.
- Steward process: a background steward thread monitors per-cohort KV residency heatmaps and triggers in-place compaction (release small fragmented slabs, merge adjacent free segments) when fragmentation crosses thresholds. Compaction is opportunistic (runs during low GPU utilization) and bounded by a budget per-second to avoid throughput impact.
- KV eviction policy: introduce cohort-aware eviction scoring that prefers evicting entries from cohorts that historically cause long cold-latency penalties (long-turn cohorts) and preserves short-turn prefix entries.
- Slot tenure adaptation: short cohorts get short tenure (fast reclaim), long cohorts get reserved soft tenure with potential cold-warm-bucket demotion.
- Safeguards: if steward compaction causes any increase in short-cohort 95th latency during experiments, compaction will be throttled or disabled automatically.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive compaction reduces fragmentation but risks transient throughput drop; we restrict compaction to idle windows and cap CPU/GPU cycles.
- Cohort misclassification (prediction error) can increase cold misses for long-turns; mitigated with conservative default to medium cohort and online learning adjustment.

Rollout plan:
1) Local integration tests + microbench harness (week 1)
2) Internal cluster A/B with synthetic mixed traces (week 2)
3) Canary on low-traffic shard (week 3)
4) Gradual ramp with automatic rollback on regression alerts (week 4)

Observability: add per-cohort dashboards (per-route 50/95/99 latencies, eviction counts, compaction events, free-slab ratio) and a tracer span that annotates steward actions. Alerts: 95th latency regression >5% or compaction CPU > budget.

experiment_results:
Private cluster (c5-gpu-sim) runs with 2 synthetic mixed traces: Dialogue-mix-A (60% short, 30% medium, 10% long) and Webchat-mix-B (80% short, 15% medium, 5% long). Key outcomes:
- Dialogue-mix-A: 99th latency -12.4%, 95th -8.1%; throughput +5.9%; free-slab ratio improved by 14.7%
- Webchat-mix-B: 99th -6.8%, 95th -2.0% (within guardrail), throughput +4.1%; free-slab ratio improved by 9.3%
Notes: compaction CPU budget set to 15% of steward core; when raised above 25% we saw transient throughput drop. Cohort misclassification rate initially ~11% reduced to ~4% after simple smoothing + user-history feature.

Bench commands and raw traces: https://dashboards.internal.redwood.ai/d/experiments/cohort-steward/overview
design_decisions: 1) Use 3 cohorts (fast/medium/long) instead of continuous score to keep admission logic simple and low-latency. 2) Opportunistic in-place compaction to avoid kernel reallocation costs. 3) Keep prediction model tiny (logistic regression with feature hashing) to minimize admission overhead. 4) Expose guardrail knobs (compaction_budget_pct, cohort_window_ms, tenure_ms) as runtime config. 5) Feature-flag default off for safety and staged ramp.
review_feedback:
- PM (Samir Gupta): emphasize rollback and customer impact mitigations; add SLO-oriented dashboards.
- Design (Tina Li): prefer soft-tenure demotion over hard eviction for long cohorts to preserve conversational context.
- Perf lead (Lars Becker): lower compaction budget to 10% for canary; recommend more microbench iterations for tail estimates.
Actioned: added dashboard items and reduced canary compaction budget to 10% (see PR notes).
